Fig. 8: Comparison of bias correction predictions generated with StormNet and a sequential LSTM-based approach (”LSTM”) [77] for Hurricane Idalia (2023). Gauge stations in which StormNet (LSTM) yields better performance are denoted with purple (yellow), while larger (smaller) data point radii represent greater (lower) values of RMSE for the considered station. Each station is represented only by the model that yields the lowest RMSE (i.e., the best model). The gray-outlined dark blue line indicates the storm track. 24 h- and 36 h-ahead predictions are shown in (a, b) and (c, d), respectively. Predictions for the full test dataset are shown in (a, c) while predictions for a 2-day period around landfall are shown in (b, d).

Fig. 1: Overview of the proposed spatio-temporal learning pipeline for bias correction in hurricane storm surge forecasting StormNet. (A) Data preprocessing: include computation of offsets between modeled and observed water levels at each gauge station. (B) Graph computation: construction of the spatio-temporal graph G = (V, E), where nodes represent stations and edges represent correlations betweeen stations. (C) Offset prediction: the proposed StormNet model forecasts future offsets ôi(t), which are subsequently used to correct the physics-based (ADCIRC) modeled water levels.
